Bee or wasp sting: scrape the stinger out sideways with a fingernail or the edge of a card; don't use tweezers. Wash the area with soap and water and hold a cold cloth or wrapped ice pack on it for 20 minutes. Watch for an allergic reaction: swelling of the lips, mouth, tongue or throat, trouble breathing or swallowing, sudden confusion, dizziness or fainting. If that happens, use their adrenaline auto-injector if they have one, and a second one after 5 minutes if they're not better. Have them lie down (sit up slowly if breathing is hard) and don't let them stand or walk. Call emergency services now if any sign of an allergic reaction appears, and say it may be anaphylaxis.

Source: NHS, Insect bites and stings; NHS, Anaphylaxis. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

In an emergency, call your local emergency number (911 in the US, 112 in Europe).
